paper_sections.title: Longitudinal changes in rsFC following CBT

description.value: A resting-state functional connectivity study examined baseline depression severity, longitudinal changes following cognitive behavioral therapy, and prediction of treatment outcome in patients with major depressive disorder using anterior subcallosal cingulate, rostral anterior cingulate, and Brodmann's area 25 seeds.

spans.text: In the current study, using resting state fMRI (rsfMRI) data from the same set of subjects, we used the rACC, and two subregions of the SCC (BA25 and aSCC) as seeds and examined (a) correlates of depression symptom severity in MDD at baseline; (b) correlations between longitudinal changes in rsFC and clinical improvement; and (c) prediction of treatment outcome with CBT using baseline rsFC.

value: We anticipated that anterior cingulate rsFC with frontoparietal regions would be negatively correlated with depression severity at baseline, would predict CBT outcome, and would increase as a function of improvement following CBT.

description.value: Patients with current major depressive disorder received 14 sessions of cognitive behavioral therapy over approximately 12 weeks, with resting-state fMRI and Beck Depression Inventory assessments before and after treatment. Healthy volunteers were scanned at two timepoints without intervention. The study was not randomized to treatment modalities.

For pre > post comparisons, positive (negative) t-values denote group averaged reductions (increases) in FC following treatment. For pre > post versus change in BDI, negative t-values denote regions which exhibit greater rsFC decreases with greater improvement, whereas positive t-values denote regions which exhibit greater rsFC increases (or less decreases) with greater improvement.
